channel.title: The Fox News Rundown
channel.description: The FOX News Rundown is your daily news podcast for making sense of the big issues directly impacting your life. Go beyond the headlines every morning and join some of FOX News’ most exceptional journalists—including FOX News Channel reporters Peter Doocy, Aishah Hasnie, Bill Melugin, Alex Hogan, Lucas Tomlinson and Jacqui Heinrich and FOX News Radio reporters Dave Anthony, Jessica Rosenthal, Lisa Brady, and Gurnal Scott - as they tap into the global reporting resources of FOX News and get unparalleled political analysis and exclusive insight from top newsmakers. The Rundown offers a sharp contrast of perspectives you won’t hear anywhere else, and a daily commentary you can't miss, we deliver the full picture of the day's biggest events.

item.title: Targeting the Kingdom: How El Chapo Was Caught & the Fight Against Fentanyl
item.description: Fentanyl overdose deaths are seeing a significant drop, but is the battle against cartels really turning the tide? A former federal special agent joins the Rundown to explain why targeting leadership alone acts like "whack-a-mole" unless financial communication networks are completely dismantled.FOX's Jessica Rosenthal speaks with Retired Special Agent with Homeland Security Investigations Eric Balliet to analyze the latest overdose statistics, effectiveness of border strategies and what it takes to disrupt transnational criminal networks. item.title: Flipping NY Red? Bruce Blakeman on ICE, Sanctuary Cities, and Data Centers
item.description:
Could New York have a Republican governor for the first time in nearly 20 years? Nassau County Executive and New York Republican gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman breaks down his campaign strategy to flip the Empire State. Blakeman sharply criticizes Governor Kathy Hochul's policies in ICE cooperation, sanctuary status, and economic growth, arguing current leadership endangers public safety and drives away jobs. He outlines his day-one priorities if elected, including signing an executive order to end New York's sanctuary state status, lowering utility bills, and cutting taxes.
Is AI an existential threat or the engine of America’s next economic boom?With the national debate reaching a fever pitch ahead of the midterms, Washington and Silicon Valley are locked in a high-stakes battle over regulation versus innovation. FOX Business host Taylor Riggs joins the Rundown to preview her upcoming special, "FOX Business In Depth: AI Arms Race." She breaks down the line between real public safety risks and massive economic potential—and exposes why Big Tech's doomsday "scare tactics" might come with ulterior motives.
PLUS, commentary by Dr. Marc Siegel, Senior Medical Analyst for FOX News.

item.title: Voice Clones & Crime Compounds: The Shocking Scale (and Cost) of AI Cybercrime
item.description:
Cybercrime is reaching record proportions, with older Americans losing tens of billions of dollars to sophisticated online schemes. But this isn’t just about hackers stealing passwords—bad actors are using artificial intelligence to clone voices, replicate family photos, and manipulate victims into willingly handing over their savings.
Heritage Foundation Chief Economist E.J. Antoni joined Lisa Brady on the FOX News Rundown earlier this week to explain how massive overseas crime compounds in Southeast Asia—often operated using trafficked forced labor—are running these scams like full-scale businesses. Antoni outlined why targeting bank transactions happens too late, why tech companies must partner with government agencies to stop fraud at the source, and the steps families can take to protect themselves online.
We couldn't air the entire conversation earlier this week due to time constraints, but you can hear it in full on today's FOX News Rundown: Extra.

item.title: Capitol Shakeup: How The Midterms Could Upend Congressional Leadership
item.description:
With the midterm elections growing closer, the future of Congressional leadership is top of mind as Democrats eye potential control of the House and Senate this November. FOX News Chief Congressional Correspondent Chad Pergram joins the Rundown to discuss potential outcomes following Election Day if Republicans lose one or both of their razor-thin majorities.
Plus, anchor of Fox's The Story and host of The Untold Story podcast Martha MacCallum breaks down what the latest Fox News Power Rankings mean for the midterms and reflects on Fox News' industry impact as the network celebrates its 30th anniversary.

item.title: Is College Still Worth It? Purdue’s Mitch Daniels on Rising Tuitions, AI & Declining Trust
item.description:
Today, on the FOX News Rundown: Extra podcast, we ask: As Americans lose confidence in higher education, is the traditional four-year college degree losing its value? Earlier this week, former Indiana Governor and Purdue University Interim President Mitch Daniels joined the FOX News Rundown to break down why tuition costs, political indoctrination, and the rise of AI are driving a historic decline in trust.
Daniels also explained to host Lisa Brady how Purdue has frozen tuition since 2012, why trade schools are gaining ground, and what universities must do to survive. In addition, he weighed in on school safety and accountability concerns in light of the shocking assault allegations at Cornell University.
We couldn't air the entire conversation earlier this week due to time constraints, but you can hear it in full on today's FOX News Rundown: Extra.

item.title: Data Centers, Tariffs, and Affordability: The Issues Driving Races in Ohio and Maine
item.description:
As rising data center energy demands drive up utility costs nationwide, energy affordability has emerged as a key midterm issue—especially in Ohio. Republican-led legislation intended to prevent Big Tech companies from shifting infrastructure costs to consumers was blocked by Senate Democrats, who argued the bill was ineffective. Ohio Republican Senator Jon Husted joins the Rundown to discuss his Ratepayer Protection Act, the political battle over data centers, and how affordability concerns are influencing voters ahead of Election Day—especially in his own tight election race.
 Plus, Colby College political science professors Nick Jacobs and Daniel Shea break down the fiercely contested Maine Senate race between Republican Susan Collins and Democrat Troy Jackson. Fresh off the candidates' recent debates, they analyze how rising heating oil prices, tariffs, and wider cost-of-living struggles are weighing on voters.
